source_basis.note: Original educational training content for the SIH prototype, informed by DGMS statutory/safety material. It is not a substitute for mine-specific SOPs, statutory training, or competent safety review.
source_basis.primary_reference: DGMS Mines Safety & allied Legislation, including the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 and Mine Rescue Rules, 1985.

modules.title: Emergency Evacuation & Fire Safety
modules.description: Recognize emergency warnings, follow the site's emergency communication and evacuation arrangements, and reach the designated safe area without taking unnecessary risks.

lessons.title: Recognizing an Industrial Emergency
lessons.content:
An industrial emergency can involve fire, smoke, equipment failure, a major roof or ground incident, loss of ventilation, or another event requiring people to move to safety. The first priority is protecting people and following the mine or workplace emergency plan.

When an alarm, emergency announcement, or other authorized warning is received, stop normal work safely, pay attention to instructions, and use the designated communication and evacuation arrangements. Do not ignore an alarm because the situation is not yet obvious.

Always follow the site's current emergency plan, escape-route markings, assembly arrangements, and instructions from authorized personnel.

lessons.title: Safe Evacuation Awareness
lessons.content:
Evacuation should be orderly and based on the designated escape routes and emergency procedures for the site. Workers should keep awareness of their surroundings, avoid unnecessary delay, and report to the designated assembly or safe area.

Do not return to an affected area simply to collect belongings or equipment. Do not leave the designated safe area until authorized personnel give further instructions.

The exact escape route, assembly point, alarm signal, and emergency communication method are site-specific and must be learned during workplace training.

lessons.title: Fire Hazard Awareness
lessons.content:
Fire prevention begins with recognizing hazards and reporting unsafe conditions. Examples include damaged electrical equipment, overheating machinery, combustible material accumulation, or other conditions identified by the site's risk assessment.

In an emergency, use only the response actions you have been trained and authorized to perform. If the situation is beyond your training or the emergency procedure calls for evacuation, prioritize evacuation and notification rather than attempting an unsafe intervention.

Fire response equipment and procedures vary by workplace, so the simulator teaches decision-making rather than replacing site-specific emergency training.

drill.title: Emergency Evacuation Drill
drill.description: Practice recognizing an emergency warning and choosing the safe response path in a simulated mining environment.
drill.instructions: Identify the warning, follow the designated safe route shown by the simulation, avoid returning to the affected area, and finish at the designated safe/assembly point.
drill.scenario: A simulated mine emergency requires workers to leave the affected area and reach the designated safe location.
drill.safety_action: Follow the site's emergency procedure, use the designated escape route, report to the safe/assembly area, and wait for authorization before further movement.

questions.question: Why should workers avoid returning to an affected area after evacuation?
questions.option_a: Because personal belongings are never important
questions.option_b: Because re-entry may expose them to the continuing hazard

questions.option_a: The designated escape route and assembly arrangement

modules.title: Mine Tunnel & Hazardous Gas Safety
modules.description: Understand why ventilation, gas monitoring, warning signs, communication, and controlled response are essential in underground mine environments.

lessons.title: Underground Tunnel Hazards
lessons.content:
Underground workings can present hazards associated with ventilation, ground conditions, fire, machinery, and hazardous atmospheres. Workers must follow the mine's approved operating procedures and emergency arrangements.

The DGMS has emphasized the importance of maintaining ventilation arrangements and preserving an available means of egress during emergencies. Ventilation problems can contribute to unsafe atmospheric conditions, so changes or damage to ventilation controls must be handled through authorized mine procedures.

lessons.title: Hazardous Atmosphere Awareness
lessons.content:
A hazardous atmosphere may not always be obvious from appearance alone. Gas monitoring and the mine's ventilation system are therefore important parts of underground safety.

Workers should take alarms and abnormal readings seriously, follow the site's response procedure, and move to a safe location when instructed. Do not enter or remain in an area that the site's procedure identifies as unsafe.

The specific gas limits, instruments, alarm settings, and authorized response actions must come from the applicable mine rules and site procedures.

lessons.title: Ventilation and Emergency Response
lessons.content:
Ventilation helps control the underground atmosphere and supports safe working conditions. DGMS guidance highlights the importance of maintaining ventilation arrangements and avoiding unauthorized disturbance of ventilation controls.

If ventilation is disrupted or an atmospheric warning occurs, workers should follow the mine's emergency procedure, communicate the condition through the approved reporting chain, and move to the designated safe area when required. Only trained and authorized personnel should carry out technical ventilation interventions.

drill.title: Mine Tunnel Emergency Drill
drill.description: Practice responding to a simulated tunnel hazard and atmospheric warning without entering or remaining in an unsafe area.
drill.instructions: Recognize the tunnel warning, follow the simulation's designated safe response, avoid the unsafe zone, and report/complete the drill as instructed.
drill.scenario: A simulated underground tunnel develops a hazardous condition and the worker must follow the approved emergency response.
drill.safety_action: Take the warning seriously, follow the mine's emergency procedure, avoid the unsafe area, communicate the condition through the approved chain, and wait for authorized instructions.

questions.question: Why is ventilation important in underground workings?
questions.option_a: It is only needed for comfort
questions.option_b: It helps maintain safe atmospheric conditions and control hazards
questions.option_d: It is used only after an incident

questions.question: What should a worker do after an atmospheric warning or abnormal reading?
questions.option_a: Treat it as unimportant if the tunnel looks normal
questions.option_b: Follow the site's approved response procedure
questions.option_c: Continue deeper into the affected area

questions.question: Who should perform technical ventilation interventions?
questions.option_b: Only trained and authorized personnel under the applicable procedure

questions.question: Why should ventilation controls not be disturbed without authorization?
questions.option_a: Ventilation changes can affect underground atmospheric conditions and safety

questions.question: Can a hazardous atmosphere always be identified visually?
questions.option_a: Yes, because every hazardous gas is visible
questions.option_b: No, visual appearance alone is not a reliable safety check

questions.question: What should happen when a worker is instructed to leave an unsafe tunnel area?
questions.option_a: Remain there until the warning disappears
questions.option_b: Follow the approved evacuation or safe-movement procedure

questions.question: Why is communication important during a tunnel emergency?
questions.option_a: It helps the approved response process receive information about the hazard
questions.option_b: It removes the need for evacuation
questions.option_c: It guarantees the hazard has ended

questions.question: What is the main learning objective of the tunnel AR drill?
questions.option_a: Practice safe decision-making around a simulated tunnel hazard
